Dependent on a root-dhamma, a root-dhamma arises by way of root-condition:

dependent on non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion arise; dependent on non-hatred, non-greed and non-delusion arise; dependent on non-delusion, non-greed and non-hatred arise; dependent on greed, delusion arises; dependent on delusion, greed arises;

dependent on hatred, delusion arises; dependent on delusion, hatred arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so forth] … *Hetuṁ dhammaṁ paṭicca hetu dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā—alobhaṁ paṭicca adoso amoho, adosaṁ paṭicca alobho amoho, amohaṁ paṭicca alobho adoso, lobhaṁ paṭicca moho, mohaṁ paṭicca lobho, dosaṁ paṭicca moho, mohaṁ paṭicca doso; paṭisandhikkhaṇe …pe…*

dependent on non-greed (*alobha*), non-hatred (*adosa*), and non-delusion (*amoha*), the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise (the cycle). Dependent on greed (*lobha*) ... [etc. ...
Delusion and the aggregates associated with it, and mind-produced matter …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe….

Dependent on a non-root phenomenon, root and non-root phenomena arise by way of root condition:

2.1.1.2–6. The Chapter on Co-nascence Condition, Support, Conjoined, and Associated (The Chapter on Co-nascence, the Chapter on Conditions, and the Chapter on Support have questions identical to those in the Chapter on Dependent [Paṭicca-vāra]. Regarding the Great Elements...).

When they are completed, the phrase “conditioned by the basis” (*vatthuṃ paccayā*) should be applied. The five bases (*pañcāyatanāni*) should be formulated in such a way that they are obtained both in the direct order (*anuloma*) and in the reverse order (*paccanīya*).
The combination of associated factors (*saṃsaṭṭhavāra*) and the combination of conjoined factors (*sampayuttavāra*) are complete. There is no form; there is only the formless (*arūpa*).

Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Root Condition (Hetu)

A cause-condition phenomenon is related to a cause-condition phenomenon by way of the root-cause condition (*hetupaccaya*): non-greed is related to non-hatred and non-delusion by way of the root-cause condition (the cycle).
Greed is related to delusion by way of the root-cause condition; hatred is related to delusion by way of the root-cause condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... and so forth.

A root-phenomenon is a condition for a non-root phenomenon by way of the root-condition: roots are a condition by way of the root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter; at the moment of rebirth-linking ...
[etc. ... A root-phenomenon is a condition for both a root-phenomenon and a non-root-phenomenon by way of the root-condition:
non-greed is a condition by way of the root-condition for non-hatred, non-delusion, their associated aggregates, and mind-produced matter.
Condition. (The Wheel. Greed is a condition for delusion ... [etc. ... at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... Object-Condition.
A state that is a root-condition is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a root-condition: taking a root-condition as an object, root-conditions arise.
A root phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-root phenomenon: taking a root [phenomenon] as object, non-root aggregates arise.
A root phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for both a root and a non-root phenomenon: taking a root [phenomenon] as object, both roots and associated aggregates arise.
A non-root phenomenon is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-root phenomenon: having given a gift, [observing] virtue... [etc.]... [arises].
Having performed an Uposatha ceremony, one reviews it; one reviews former good deeds.

Having emerged from jhāna …pe… noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, the fruit …pe… Nibbāna …pe… Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage, purification, the path, the fruit, and adverting by way of object-condition.
The Noble Ones review defilements that have been abandoned by way of non-causality, they review defilements that have been suppressed, and they know defilements previously practiced.
[They review] the eye …pe… the physical basis (vatthu); they contemplate the aggregates as impermanent by way of non-causality …pe… sorrow arises;
with the divine eye one sees a form, with the divine ear-element one hears a sound, and with the knowledge of penetration of minds …pe… [they know the mind].

One does not know the mind of one who possesses a non-causal mind. The base of infinite space [is not known] by the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the base of nothingness [is not known] by the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe… the visible-form base [is not known] by eye-consciousness …pe… the tangible-object base [is not known] by body-consciousness …pe… the aggregates that are non-causal [are not known] by the knowledge of the modes of psychic power,
the knowledge of others' minds, or the knowledge of recollecting past lives.
[It is] a condition for the knowledge of the destiny according to deeds, the knowledge of future existences, and advertence, by way of object-condition.
A non-root state is a condition for a root state by way of object-condition: having given a gift. (The first course alone;

States that are both roots and non-roots are related to a state that is a root by way of the object condition: taking as object the aggregates associated with the roots and the roots themselves, the roots arise.

States that are both roots and non-roots are related to a state that is not a root by way of the object condition: taking as object the aggregates associated with the roots and the roots themselves, the non-root aggregates arise.

States that are both roots and non-roots are a condition, by way of object-condition, for states that are both root and non-root: taking as object both the roots and the associated aggregates, both the roots and the associated aggregates arise.
Predominance:
A state that is a root is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is a root—namely, object-predominance and co-nascent predominance.
Object-predominance: Taking a cause as estimable, causes arise. Co-nascent predominance:
A cause that is a predominant factor is related to its associated causes by way of the predominance condition.
A causal state is related to a non-causal state by way of the predominance condition: namely, object-predominance and co-nascent predominance.
Object-predominance: Taking a cause as an object and esteeming it, non-causal aggregates arise. Co-nascent predominance:
A cause that is a predominant factor is related to its associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of the predominance condition.
A causal state is related to both a causal and a non-causal state by way of the predominance condition—namely, object-predominance.
Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: taking the root-cause as an object and esteeming it, the root-causes and the associated aggregates arise.
Co-nascent predominance: the root-cause as predominance is a condition, by way of the predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates, for the root-causes, and for mind-produced matter.
A state that is not a root-cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state that is not a root-cause: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance.
Object-predominance: having given a gift... (to be expanded in detail up to: ...the aggregates that are not root-causes. Conascence-predominance:
a predominance that is not a root-cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

A state that is neither-root nor rootless is a condition, by way of association-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor rootless: one aggregate that is neither-root nor rootless is [a condition] for three aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
Dissociation:
A state that is neither-root but has roots is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor rootless: [by way of] conascence, … [etc. … [end of section].
Postnascent: Co-nascent aggregates that are not roots but are accompanied by roots are related to mind-produced matter by way of dissociation condition;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... Postnascent aggregates that are not roots but are accompanied by roots are related to this prenascent body by way of dissociation condition.
A state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause:
namely, conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. As conascence: non-causal, causeless aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... the aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for the physical heart-base.
Condition: The [heart-]base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*). As pre-arisen:

the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the [heart-]base is a condition for the rootless-with-rooted aggregates by way of dissociation-condition.
As post-arisen: the rootless, non-rooted aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation-condition.
A state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for a state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause:

namely, conascence and prenascence. As conascence: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for the aggregates (khandhas) that are neither causes nor accompanied by causes.
As prenascence: the physical basis is a condition, by way of dissociation-condition, for the aggregates that are neither causes nor accompanied by causes.

A non-root dhamma with root is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a non-root dhamma with root: one non-root aggregate with root is a condition for three aggregates … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
A non-root dhamma with root is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a non-root dhamma without root: [by way of] conascence, postnascence … pe ….
A non-root but root-possessing state is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for both a non-root but root-possessing state and a non-root and rootless state:
one non-root but root-possessing aggregate is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe ….
A state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for a state that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause:
namely, conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent:

One aggregate that is neither a root-cause nor accompanied by a root-cause is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter … (and so on) … up to non-percipient beings.

Pre-arisen: the eye … [and so on] … the physical basis, as impermanent … [and so on] … grief arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, a rootless, causeless resultant state arises by way of object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*);
the visible-form base for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-object base for body-consciousness … [and so on] … the eye-base … [and so on] … the body-base … the physical basis.
The aggregates that are neither-root nor rootless are related to [other] aggregates that are neither-root nor rootless by way of presence condition.

Postnascent aggregates that are neither-root nor rootless are related to the prenascent [body]... [and so on]. Edible food is related to this body... [and so on]. The material life-faculty is related to kamma-produced matter by way of presence condition.
A state that is neither-root nor rootless is a condition, by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*), for a state that is neither-root nor rooted:

namely, conascence (*sahajāta*) and prenascence (*purejāta*). As conascence: at the moment of rebirth-linking, the [heart-]base is a presence-condition for the aggregates that are neither-root nor rooted.
As prenascence: the eye ... [and so on] ... the base is contemplated as impermanent ... [and so on] ... and grief arises; [likewise] regarding wholesome and unwholesome states.
When [the mind] has ceased, the resultant state, which is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause, arises with that as its object;

one sees a form with the divine eye and hears a sound with the divine ear-element. Base-prenascence: the base is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for the aggregates that are neither causes nor accompanied by a cause.

States that are neither-cause nor with-cause, and states that are neither-cause nor without-cause, are related to a state that is neither-cause but with-cause by way of presence condition (atthipaccaya)—namely, conascence (sahajāta) and prenascence (purejāta).
As to conascence: one aggregate that is neither-cause but with-cause, together with the [heart-]base, is related to three aggregates ...
pe ... at the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... one aggregate that is neither-cause but with-cause, together with the [heart-]base, is related to three aggregates ... pe ....

States that are neither-cause nor with-cause, and states that are neither-cause nor without-cause, are related to a state that is neither-cause nor without-cause by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*):
namely, conascence, post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. As conascence:
non-causal aggregates accompanied by cause and the great elements are related to mind-produced matter by way of presence condition; likewise at the moment of rebirth-linking.
… [as before] … Postnascent aggregates that are not roots but are associated with roots, and edible food, are a condition by way of presence-condition for this body.
Postnascent aggregates that are not roots but are associated with roots, and the material life-faculty, are a condition by way of presence-condition for kamma-produced matter. … [as before] …

In the Pure Object condition there are four; in the predominance condition there are four; in the proximity condition there are four; in the contiguity condition there are four; in the conascence condition...
Seven in mutuality, six in reciprocal conditionality, seven in support condition, four in decisive support condition, two in prenascence,
two in postnascence, two in repetition, four in kamma, four in result, four in nutriment, four in faculty, four in jhāna, three in path,
two in association, three in dissociation, seven in presence, [seven] in absence...
Four in the case of the dissociated, four in the case of the non-dissociated, seven in the case of the non-dissociated—thus should it be counted.
This is the Positive Order.

A state that is not a root but has roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor has roots; it is a condition by way of co-nascence-condition; it is a condition by way of decisive-support-condition; it is a condition by way of kamma-condition.
A state that is not a root but has roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a root nor has roots;

it is a condition by way of co-nascence-condition; it is a condition by way of decisive-support-condition; it is a condition by way of postnascence-condition; it is a condition by way of kamma-condition.

A state that is neither-root nor has-root is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state that is neither-root nor has-root, and for a state that is neither-root nor rootless; it is also a condition, by way of kamma condition.
A state that is neither-root nor rootless is a condition, by way of object condition, for a state that is neither-root nor rootless;
it is also a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, by way of decisive support condition, by way of prenascence condition, and by way of postnascence condition.
Condition ... by way of nutriment-condition ... by way of faculty-condition.

A state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root; it is a condition by way of conascence-condition; it is a condition by way of decisive-support-condition; it is a condition by way of prenascence-condition.

States that are both neither-root and accompanied-by-root, and states that are neither-root nor accompanied-by-root, are [conditions] by way of conascence and prenascence for a state that is neither-root nor accompanied-by-root.

States that are neither-cause nor with-cause, and states that are neither-cause nor without-cause, are related to a state that is neither-cause nor without-cause by way of conascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty.
